extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Congress, federal department heads, and senior military commanders (1861–1862)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of President Lincoln's wartime messages, orders, and correspondence (late 1861–Jan 1862) giving policy directives, operational orders, and recommendations to Congress and military leaders. Includes proclamations, strategic guidance, administrative recommendations, and specific conditions for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an agricultural and statistical bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: An agricultural and statistical bureau might profitably be organized; annual reports exhibiting the condition of our agriculture, commerce, and manufactures would present a fund of information of great practical value to the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed plan specified; recommended that Congress consider whether something more than a clerkship can be given voluntarily for general advantage; annual reports to inform policy and public knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of laws suppressing the African slave trade
rubrics_metrics.description: The execution of the laws for the suppression of the African slave trade has been confided to the Department of the Interior; recent efforts have been attended with unusual success—vessels fitted out for the slave trade seized and condemned, and persons convicted, including one capitally convicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites concrete enforcement outcomes (seizures, convictions, penalties) as measures of success; implies continued executive oversight and prosecution under existing law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of persons liberated under the confiscation act
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act entitled 'An act to confiscate property used for insurrectionary purposes' the legal claims of certain persons to the labor and service of certain other persons have become forfeited, and numbers of the latter thus liberated are already dependent on the United States, and must be provided for in some way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend that Congress provide for accepting such persons from States (according to some mode of valuation) in lieu of direct taxes or by other agreement; that such persons, on acceptance by the General Government, be at once deemed free; and that steps be taken for colonizing them at places with a congenial climate. Consider including free colored people desiring colonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire territory and appropriate funds to carry out colonization
rubrics_metrics.description: To carry out the plan of colonization may involve the acquiring of territory, and also the appropriation of money beyond that to be expended in the territorial acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues constitutional power to acquire territory is established by practice (cites Louisiana purchase); presents expediency and perceived necessity as justification; invites Congressional consideration of appropriations and territorial acquisition as part of colonization plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Union as the primary object; avoid unnecessary radical measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the integrity of the Union prominent as the primary object of the contest, leaving all questions which are not of vital military importance to the more deliberate action of the Legislature. Adhere to the blockade and to the act of Congress to confiscate property used for insurrectionary purposes; avoid hasty adoption of radical and extreme measures which may reach the loyal as well as the disloyal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise prudence and obedience to existing statutes; new laws on subjects such as confiscation will be considered if proposed, but refrain from measures that indiscriminately affect loyal citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized military command under a single general-in-chief
rubrics_metrics.description: An army is better directed by a single mind (even if inferior) than by two superior ones at variance and cross-purposes with each other; in joint operations those engaged must have a common end and a single controlling mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports designation of a single general-in-chief (here, General McClellan) and urges that the nation and subordinates give him confidence and cordial support; warns against divided authority leading to failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic principle: menace multiple points and seize weakened ones
rubrics_metrics.description: We have the greater numbers and the enemy has the greater facility of concentrating forces; we must menace him with superior forces at different points at the same time so that we can safely attack one or both if he makes no change; if he weakens one to strengthen the other, forbear to attack the strengthened one, but seize and hold the weakened one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by hypothetical Winchester/Manassas scenario and applied to coordination between Buell and Halleck (menace Columbus while another threatens Bowling Green/East Tennessee); emphasizes flexibility and exploiting enemy redistribution rather than attacking on exterior lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for release of prisoners in Maryland
rubrics_metrics.description: Prisoners previously arrested in Maryland and detained in military custody by the President's authority are to be released on conditions: (1) if they held civil or military offices when arrested and the terms have expired, they shall not resume or reclaim such office; and (2) all persons availing themselves must engage by oath or parole of honor to maintain the Union and the Constitution and to in no way aid the insurrection by arms, counsel, conversation, or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly excludes prisoners of war from the proclamation; establishes parole/oath as formal condition for civilian detainee release and imposes office-resumption restriction where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter a merchant vessel to transport exhibits to London (1862)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that authority be given to charter a suitable merchant vessel to take articles which persons in this country may wish to exhibit at the industrial exhibition to be held in London in 1862, since no naval vessel can be spared for the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to provide facilities similar to the government exhibition of 1851; transmittal of committee correspondence and circulars to Congress for early consideration due to timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to suspend the writ of habeas corpus in specific case
rubrics_metrics.description: You or any officer you may designate will in your discretion suspend the writ of habeas corpus so far as may relate to Major Chase, alleged to be guilty of treasonable practices against this government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegates discretionary authority to the commanding general (McClellan) for a named individual; serves as precedent for case-specific suspension under executive/military discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: General War Order No. 1: coordinate a nationwide movement and hold leaders accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered that 22 February 1862 be the day for a general movement of the land and naval forces of the United States against the insurgent forces; specified armies and naval forces be ready; that all other forces obey existing orders and be ready to obey additional orders when duly given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heads of departments, especially Secretaries of War and Navy, and all commanders and subordinates will be severally held to their strict and full responsibilities for the prompt execution of this order; lists specific armies and theaters to prepare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special War Order No. 1: form expedition from Army of the Potomac to seize point near Manassas
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered that all the disposable force of the Army of the Potomac, after providing safely for the defence of Washington, be formed into an expedition for the immediate object of seizing and occupying a point upon the railroad southwestward of what is known as Manassas Junction; details to be in the discretion of the commander-in-chief and the expedition to move before or on 22 February next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets mission objective, preserves operational discretion to commander-in-chief, and ties timing to the general movement date; requires protection of Washington before committing disposable forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-of-command assignment for the 'Lane Expedition'
rubrics_metrics.description: The expedition commonly called the 'Lane Expedition' shall be, as much as has been promised at the adjutant-general's office, under the supervision of General McClellan, and not any more; General Lane has been told that he is under the command of General Hunter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies supervisory authority to avoid confusion; directs expedition size and character—'not a great, exhausting affair, but a snug, sober column of 10,000 or 15,000.' Emphasizes that Lane is subject to Hunter's command per appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require coordination and timely commitment among field commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to Buell and Halleck urging them to be in concert and to name as early a day as safely possible on or before which they can be ready to move southward in concert; delay is ruining us and it is indispensable to have something definite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated telegraphs and letters instruct coordination; suggests simultaneous movements (e.g., feigned or real attack upon Columbus) to prevent enemy reinforcement; stresses that lack of coordination risks strategic failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and recognition for retiring and appointed senior generals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend consideration of what further mark of recognition is due to General Scott upon retirement, and emphasize that the designation of General McClellan is, in considerable degree, the selection of the country as well as of the Executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for public confidence and cordial support for appointed commanders to enable their efficient service; links national honor and morale to recognition of senior officers.
